dossier.purpose: skills-ref is the Python reference library and CLI (subdirectory skills-ref/ of the agentskills/agentskills repo) for the Agent Skills format. It finds SKILL.md in a skill directory, parses the YAML frontmatter, checks the name/description/compatibility/field rules, prints properties as JSON, and generates an <available_skills> XML catalog block (name, description, SKILL.md path) for agent system prompts. Its README labels it demonstration-only. The surrounding repo holds the format specification (docs/specification.mdx), a Mintlify documentation site, a client showcase, and contributor/agent guidance. It ships no skills: the tree contains no SKILL.md files, and CONTRIBUTING.md says no directory of community skills is maintained. Per-task loading of skills (progressive disclosure) is described as client-agent behaviour and is not implemented in this repo.

claims.claim: A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file (metadata with name and description at minimum, plus instructions); skills can also bundle scripts, reference materials, templates and other resources.
Skills package procedural knowledge into portable, version-controlled folders that agents load on demand (domain expertise, repeatable workflows, cross-product reuse).

Agents load skills through progressive disclosure in three stages: Discovery (only name+description at startup), Activation (full SKILL.md read when a task matches), Execution (optionally run bundled code or load referenced files). 'Full instructions load only when a task calls for them, so agents can keep many skills on hand with only a small context footprint.'
Agent Skills are supported by a large number of AI tools and agentic clients; see the Client Showcase.
Example skills are linked externally (https://github.com/anthropics/skills); the README does not host or list skills.
The format was originally developed by Anthropic, released as an open standard, and is open to contributions per CONTRIBUTING.md.
Code in the repository is Apache 2.0; documentation is CC-BY-4.0; see individual directories for details.
skills-ref is a 'Reference library for Agent Skills'. IMPORTANT: 'This library is intended for demonstration purposes only. It is not meant to be used in production.'
On macOS/Linux, install with a venv plus `pip install -e .`, or with `uv sync`; the `skills-ref` executable is then on PATH inside the activated virtualenv.
CLI: `skills-ref validate <path>`, `skills-ref read-properties <path>` (JSON output), `skills-ref to-prompt <path-a> <path-b>` (<available_skills> XML).
Python API: `from skills_ref import validate, read_properties, to_prompt`.

`to-prompt` generates the suggested <available_skills> XML block for an agent's system prompt. The format is 'recommended for Anthropic's models, but Skill Clients may choose to format it differently'; the <location> element tells the agent where to find the full skill instructions.

install.method: pip in a venv, editable install from a source checkout (macOS/Linux). The README does not state it, but this must be run inside the skills-ref/ directory where pyproject.toml lives.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or network calls in skills-ref. Its imports are stdlib (json, sys, pathlib, html, unicodedata, dataclasses, typing) plus click and strictyaml (import grep over skills-ref/src/skills_ref/*.py). A grep over skills-ref/ for requests/urllib/httpx/socket/subprocess/telemetry found nothing except a license-text false positive. A grep of skills-ref/src for environment-variable, home-directory and skill-directory-scan APIs also found nothing. The CLI only reads the local SKILL.md (parser.py:89; validator.py:172) and writes to stdout/stderr (cli.py:45-50,70,98). No account or hosted service is required. Network is needed only at install time to fetch dependencies from PyPI (lockfile registry https://pypi.org/simple, e.g. skills-ref/uv.lock:7-8,20-21,153-155). Docs side: the docs are a Mintlify site auto-deployed on push to the default branch (docs/README.md:3,15-17); previewing needs the Mintlify CLI from npm via `npm i -g mint` or `npx mint dev` (CONTRIBUTING.md:57-63; docs/README.md:9-11; package.json:4-6). docs/docs.json contains no analytics or tracking configuration (docs/docs.json:1-66), although the hosted site's own behaviour is not visible in the repo. The docs mention 'Track activation for analytics' only as an optional feature for client implementors (docs/client-implementation/adding-skills-support.mdx:252).

code.architecture: Small single-purpose library under skills-ref/src/skills_ref/. parser.py: find_skill_md (prefers SKILL.md, then skill.md; lines 12-27), parse_frontmatter (requires a leading '---', splits with content.split('---', 2), loads YAML with strictyaml and no schema, coerces metadata keys/values to str; lines 30-64), read_properties (builds SkillProperties; only checks name/description are non-empty strings; lines 67-112). validator.py: limits name<=64, description<=1024, compatibility<=500 (lines 10-12); ALLOWED_FIELDS = name, description, license, allowed-tools, metadata, compatibility (lines 15-22); NFKC-normalised name rules (lowercase, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, isalnum-or-hyphen, directory name must match; lines 25-67); returns list[str] of errors. prompt.py: to_prompt emits <available_skills> XML with HTML-escaped name/description and the resolved SKILL.md path (lines 9-58). models.py: SkillProperties dataclass with to_dict. errors.py: SkillError -> ParseError, ValidationError. cli.py: thin Click wrapper. It operates only on explicitly supplied paths: no skill-directory discovery/scanning, no env or home-dir access, no body parsing or size checks, and no inspection of scripts/, references/ or assets/. Around it: docs/ (Mintlify site; docs/specification.mdx is declared authoritative in AGENTS.md:14-17; client-guide and skill-authoring guides; client showcase data in docs/snippets/clients.jsx), plus AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. The tree contains no SKILL.md files.

The README documents only editable installs from a source checkout (skills-ref/README.md:10-25); no PyPI or other registry publication is documented anywhere in the tree. No release workflow: there is no .github/ directory (Glob of .github/* and .github/**/* returned nothing), no YAML/CI files at all (Glob of **/*.yml,*.yaml returned none), no publish/twine/sigstore/attest/checksum settings in pyproject.toml, READMEs, CONTRIBUTING.md or AGENTS.md (grep), no CHANGELOG/RELEASE file, and the shallow clone carries no tags (.git/packed-refs lists only refs/remotes/origin/main). claim_checks.claim: Spec name rules: <=64 chars, lowercase unicode alphanumerics and hyphens, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, must match the parent directory (docs/specification.mdx:58-65).
claim_checks.evidence: validator.py:25-67 enforces each rule after NFKC normalisation. c.isalnum() admits non-Latin letters and digits (test_validator.py:165-218 covers Chinese and Russian; uppercase Russian is rejected). The directory comparison is also NFKC-normalised (validator.py:60-65).

claim_checks.claim: Spec field constraints: compatibility 'Must be 1-500 characters if provided', metadata is a string-to-string map, allowed-tools is a space-separated string (docs/specification.mdx:126,147-152,163-167).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the docs and wins. _validate_compatibility only checks the type is str and len<=500, so an empty string passes (validator.py:87-101). validate_metadata never type-checks license, metadata or allowed-tools (validator.py:118-147); the parser only coerces metadata keys/values to str (parser.py:61-62) and passes allowed-tools through untouched (parser.py:110). Read from code, not executed.

claim_checks.claim: `skills-ref validate` 'checks that your SKILL.md frontmatter is valid and follows all naming conventions' (docs/specification.mdx:243-247).
claim_checks.evidence: True for frontmatter shape and name rules (validator.py:150-177), but the check is strict. Any key outside the six ALLOWED_FIELDS is an error (validator.py:15-22,104-115; test_validator.py:120-131), whereas the client guide mentions a `disable-model-invocation` flag (adding-skills-support.mdx:226) and recommends lenient, warn-and-load validation (adding-skills-support.mdx:128-141). validate discards the body (validator.py:173): no body-size, script, references/ or assets/ checks.

claim_checks.claim: Token-cost guidance: ~100 tokens of metadata per skill at startup, SKILL.md body <5000 tokens and <500 lines recommended (docs/specification.mdx:220-224; adding-skills-support.mdx:24,184).
claim_checks.evidence: These are unmeasured guidance figures. The repo has no tokenizer or measurement code, no published measurements, and the validator does not enforce body size (validator.py:173).

risks: Scope: skills-ref is a format validator and prompt-snippet generator, not a skills collection. The tree has no SKILL.md files, CONTRIBUTING.md:46 says no directory of community skills is maintained, and README.md:50 only links an external examples repo (not opened here). No engineering or security procedures are shipped, and per-task skill loading is left to clients (README.md:30-40; docs/client-implementation/adding-skills-support.mdx:18-30).

Self-declared demo status: 'intended for demonstration purposes only... not meant to be used in production' (skills-ref/README.md:5-6; AGENTS.md:23-26). The version is 0.1.0 (skills-ref/pyproject.toml:3), CONTRIBUTING.md:40 says the direction is undecided and code contributions are not accepted, and AGENTS.md:14-17 says implementations and tests add no format requirements, so skills-ref behaviour is explicitly non-normative.

No release, provenance or CI machinery: no .github/ directory or any CI/workflow file, no tags in the clone (.git/packed-refs), no registry install documented (only editable installs from a checkout, skills-ref/README.md:10-25), no checksums/signatures/attestations, and the version is hard-coded in two places (pyproject.toml:3; __init__.py:20). The 40 tests (parser/validator/prompt only, none for cli.py) are not run by any automation in this repo, and I did not run them.
No security policy: no SECURITY.md or private vulnerability-reporting instructions anywhere in the tree; CONTRIBUTING.md:13 routes bugs to public GitHub Issues.

Skills are an instruction/code injection surface that skills-ref does not assess. The spec lets skills bundle executable scripts (docs/specification.mdx:191-198) and pre-approve tools via the experimental `allowed-tools` field (specification.mdx:163-173). The client guide warns that untrusted repositories can 'silently inject instructions into the agent's context' (adding-skills-support.mdx:89-91). validate checks only frontmatter shape and name/directory match (validator.py:150-177), with no content, script or permission scanning, and to-prompt places author-supplied descriptions into a system-prompt block (skills-ref/README.md:91; prompt.py:43-46).

Validator versus spec and client behaviour (read from code, not executed). Any frontmatter key outside {name, description, license, allowed-tools, metadata, compatibility} is an error (validator.py:15-22,104-115) even though the client guide cites a `disable-model-invocation` flag (adding-skills-support.mdx:226) and recommends lenient loading (adding-skills-support.mdx:128-141). The spec's compatibility minimum of 1 character, string-typed metadata/allowed-tools and the body-size recommendations are not enforced (validator.py:87-147,173; docs/specification.mdx:126,147-167,221-224).

Implementation quirks found by reading, not executed. parse_frontmatter uses content.split('---', 2) (parser.py:45), so a '---' inside a frontmatter value would end the frontmatter early. The <location> element in to-prompt output is not XML-escaped although name and description are (prompt.py:43,46,50-52). read_text() is called without an explicit encoding (parser.py:89; validator.py:172) although i18n skill names are supported (test_validator.py:165-218). to_prompt calls read_properties, which does not run validate (prompt.py:39; parser.py:67-112). The CLI documents only exit codes 0/1 (cli.py:35-37).
